clue.text: Become brighter and cold — king gets excited

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps
Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
up can mean excited or worked up, as in 'all up about it'

explanation.surface: Weather turns bright and chilly while a monarch gets worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that clears up turns brighter as the clouds go, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Set bed overlooking lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A bed is set up overlooking a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a noun (a clique), not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group, a set of people.

clue.text: Riot teams badly deployed, one reckons

indicators.note: badly deployed means the letters are set out in disorder

explanation.surface: Riot police are poorly stationed, someone calculates.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimator is someone who reckons or calculates a cost.

clue.text: It could be used to strike a sovereign

definitions.text: It could be used to strike
definitions.meaning: a measuring stick could be used to rap knuckles
a monarch who rules a realm

explanation.surface: A tool that might be used to hit a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is both a straight-edge once used to punish pupils and someone who reigns.

clue.text: Fuming when conduit's stolen

parts.note: piping is a conduit for water or gas
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone is furious when the pipework is stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot means extremely hot, so steaming or fuming with heat.

clue.text: Instigate storing flower in kind of cup

indicators.note: storing means one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: to stir up trouble is to instigate it
a flower is something that flows, a river, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: Someone provokes trouble while keeping a bloom in a particular cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river (a thing that flows), not a bloom. A stirrup cup is a drink handed to a rider already mounted, before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a parting drink served to riders on horseback, so the word names a sort of cup.

clue.text: Sons defrost fish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons
to melt is to defrost

explanation.surface: Boys thaw some frozen fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelt is a small silvery food fish.

clue.text: I mean to make a home — seriously!

parts.note: taken as written
near is an old word for mean or stingy
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone declares they really mean to set up house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in earnest is to be serious, so the phrase works as seriously.

clue.text: Gas causing fuss in the navy

indicators.note: in places the fuss inside the navy's letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A gas leak causes a stir in the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas.

clue.text: Aim to find money bag outside post office

indicators.note: outside means the bag goes round the post office

parts.note: a purse is a bag for money

explanation.surface: Someone tries to find a money bag left outside the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Purpose and aim both mean an intention or goal.

clue.text: Comprehensive kid gets a quid

parts.note: a tot is a small child
quid is British slang for a pound, abbreviated L from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A child at a comprehensive school is handed a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like the British state school, but it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A comprehensive survey is a total one: both adjectives mean complete and all-inclusive.

clue.text: Claimant is quiet about offer

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning
a tender is a formal offer, as in a bid

explanation.surface: Someone making a claim quietly considers a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is one who lays claim to a throne or title, so a claimant.

clue.text: Term loosely embracing a type of artist

indicators.note: embracing means the jumbled word holds the next piece inside it
loosely means the letters of the word term are arranged freely

parts.note: a brand is a type or make of goods

explanation.surface: A loose definition of a term takes in one category of painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks like part of the surface, but it is the fodder: 'loosely' turns it into REM...T, and 'embracing' wraps that round BRAND. 'type' misleads towards printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was the great Dutch painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Player finally working to perform musical piece

indicators.note: finally picks out the final letter of the word player

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
to do a play is to perform it

explanation.surface: A musician is at last ready to play a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form with a recurring main theme, so a kind of piece.

clue.text: Tenant has no right to come in

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a renter is a tenant paying rent

explanation.surface: A tenant lacks any right of entry to the property.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come in, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Trot with me and the dog

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-winger or red
me is the crossword's setter speaking

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a jog with the speaker and the hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' looks like a jog, but is short for Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter, or Irish setter, is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: It's lucky Arabs, say, do some gardening

parts.note: Arabs are a breed of horse, so an example of horses
to hoe is to weed a bed, a gardening job

explanation.surface: Lucky Arab grooms tend a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabs, say' reads as people, but means the horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: Sympathetic vibration represented on a screen

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shared feeling shown on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is the vibration one body sets up in another tuned to the same frequency.

clue.text: Sound a bell — for a knockout?

parts.note: a hum is a sound
a dinger is something that dings, as a bell does

explanation.surface: A bell rings to end a boxing bout with a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knockout' suggests boxing, but here means a stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an excellent or remarkable thing, as is a knockout in the slang sense.

clue.text: Greek writer and leading actor spot Uncle Sam

parts.note: the hero is the leading man of a drama
a dot is a spot
Uncle Sam personifies the United States, US

explanation.surface: A Greek author and a star performer notice America.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus was the ancient Greek historian, called the father of history.

clue.text: Execute Harry looking dejected

parts.note: to hang is to execute
to dog someone is to harry or pursue them

explanation.surface: A man named Harry is put to death, looking miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced or downcast, so looking dejected.

clue.text: Spare tyre I'd inflated

parts.note: a spare tyre is a roll of belly fat, so a tum
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have pumped up the spare wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare tyre' is the belly, not a car part.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumid means swollen, bloated or puffed up, as is something inflated.

clue.text: An easing of tensions after river engulfs marquee

indicators.note: engulfs means the river surrounds the next piece

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a marquee is a large tent

explanation.surface: Relations calm after a flood swamps a festival marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is a relaxation of hostility between nations.

clue.text: Half-heartedly incapacitate an aristocrat

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the doubled middle letters of the word goes

parts.note: to nobble a racehorse is to incapacitate it

explanation.surface: Someone lazily tries to disable a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' removes one of the two Bs at the heart of NOBBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the nobility, so an aristocrat by rank.

clue.text: Meat firm included in boycott

indicators.note: included in places the firm inside the boycott

parts.note: a ban is a boycott
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A meat company is caught up in a boycott.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured meat from the back or sides of a pig, so a specific example of meat.

clue.text: Impress prisoner with writing

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
script is handwriting

explanation.surface: A convict wins people over with his writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' means to force into military service, not to amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To conscript is to draft into service, the old sense of impress.

clue.text: Tory caught taking oil preparation for illness

indicators.note: taking means the two letters hold the next piece between them

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the Tory party
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up, so the letters of oil are reworked

explanation.surface: A Conservative caught using an oil remedy for a sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory and caught each give the single letter C; 'preparation for' turns OIL into OLI, which 'taking' holds between them. The surface suggests a medicine, but 'preparation' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, an illness especially of babies and horses.

clue.text: Grovel to get chromium tool

parts.note: Cr is the chemical symbol for chromium
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather

explanation.surface: Someone abases themselves to obtain a shiny metal tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl to someone is to fawn on them, so to grovel.

clue.text: Fellow keeps chalet designed for sports event

indicators.note: keeps means one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

indicators.note: designed means the letters of chalet are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A college fellow owns a chalet built for an athletics meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is an Oxbridge college fellow. 'designed' turns CHALET into ECATHL, which 'keeps' puts inside DON; the surface pretends the chalet was built for the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is a ten-event athletics competition.

clue.text: In the past Newton stored right gas

indicators.note: stored means a letter is kept inside

parts.note: ago means in the past
N is the symbol for newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Long ago Newton kept the correct gas in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, one of the elements in air.

clue.text: Comprehensive kid after information

indicators.note: after places the kid's name behind the information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a boy's name, so a kid

explanation.surface: A comprehensive pupil follows up on some facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts ERIC behind GEN although the clue names the kid first. Using a boy's name for 'kid' is loose but standard crossword practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, covering a whole class, so comprehensive.

clue.text: Increase general unrest

indicators.note: unrest suggests disturbance, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A general increase in civil disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger, so to increase.
